name: Hemp seed oil
short: Hemp seed oil can contain traces of THC. Earlier studies found urine levels above drug-screen cutoffs; a 2000 study found peaks of 1 to 49 ng/mL, and a 2019 Korean study found no positive tests.
text: The cited sources concern traces of THC in hemp seed oil and clotting measures rather than adverse events, which they did not systematically report. A 2000 laboratory study noted that earlier reports had found urine levels of a THC breakdown product well above drug-screening cutoffs after people consumed hemp seed oil products, but that THC content had since fallen considerably; in its own volunteers, given several 15 g doses, peak urine levels of the THC breakdown product ranged from 1 to 49 ng/mL (the abstract cites 50 ng/mL as the cutoff used in random drug screens, and does not say whether any volunteer screened positive while taking the oil), and all were below positive screening and confirmation cutoffs within 48 hours of stopping. A 2019 study in Korea found that normal use of hemp seed products sold there, including hemp seed oil capsules, for up to 12 weeks did not produce positive urine cannabinoid tests. In a 12-week placebo-controlled trial in 86 healthy volunteers comparing fish, flaxseed and hempseed oil capsules, none of the oils significantly changed platelet aggregation or blood lipids. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
